questions.question: What is scope?

options.value: The region of code where a declared name can be used
The range of possible int values

questions.explanation: Scope determines name visibility within the program structure.

questions.question: What is the scope of a method parameter?
questions.explanation: A parameter is local to its method invocation.

questions.question: What happens when a local variable has the same name as an instance field?

options.value: The program always fails to compile
The local name shadows the field in that scope

questions.explanation: An unqualified name resolves to the nearer declaration; this can distinguish the field.

questions.question: Which accesses the instance field when a parameter shadows it?
questions.explanation: this identifies the current receiver object.

questions.question: Can client code directly read a private field of another class?

options.value: Yes, if the variable name matches
Only after calling a getter once

questions.explanation: Private access is restricted to the declaring class.

questions.question: Can code in a class access a private field of another instance of that same class?

options.value: Only if both objects are equal
No, private is restricted to one object
Only if the field is static

questions.explanation: Java private access is class-based, not limited to one receiver instance.

questions.question: Is a local declared inside an if block normally visible after that block?

options.value: Only when the if was true

questions.explanation: Block-local scope ends with the block.
